prompt.context: Our client, Zephyr Beverages, is a division of a large consumer products company. The division produces fruit juices in three forms, all under the Zephyr name: chilled, juice boxes, and frozen concentrate. Zephyr had sales of $600 million last year, about 3% of the company's overall sales of $20 billion. The chilled segment represents $120 million in sales per year. While juice boxes and frozen concentrate have been consistently profitable, chilled juices are only breaking even in good quarters and are losing money in bad quarters. Zephyr has received a proposal from upper management to sell the chilled juices business.
prompt.question: We need to help Zephyr decide whether or not selling the chilled juices business is a good idea. What would you recommend?

clarifying_info.q: How large is the chilled beverages market?
clarifying_info.a: Chilled beverages are a $5 billion worldwide industry.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the main competitors and what are their market shares?
clarifying_info.a: The two largest players have market shares of 40% and 25% respectively. Zephyr's market share of 12% makes it third in the industry.

clarifying_info.q: How has the market been growing?
clarifying_info.a: It has been growing at GDP the last few years and is projected to continue at that growth rate.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the key customers / buyers?
clarifying_info.a: The market for chilled juices is dominated by mothers with young kids.

clarifying_info.q: How important is brand in this market?
clarifying_info.a: Brand name is important, as mothers tend to prefer reliable products. However, the brand premium must be in line with other branded products and all branded juices sell in the same price range.
This is a highly price-sensitive market that loves coupons, promotions, etc.

clarifying_info.q: What are the competitive dynamics — any new entrants or technology changes?
clarifying_info.a: This is a highly concentrated market. There has not been a lot of change, technological or otherwise, recently and there are no obvious new entrants.

clarifying_info.q: What promotional activities can competitors do that Zephyr cannot?
clarifying_info.a: The two market leaders are able to do more advertising, couponing, promotion, and trade than Zephyr is able to do. We do not know about their profitability, but assume it is positive.

clarifying_info.q: What ingredients do competitors use vs. Zephyr?
clarifying_info.a: The market leaders produce pure orange juice and blends based on citrus juices. Zephyr uses more elaborate blends, usually with a base of pear or peach juice (95% of inputs) and flavors with cranberries, bananas, mangoes, etc. (the other 5%). Pear and peach juice are similarly priced to orange juice, but the other flavorings cost about twice as much.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Zephyr produce its products?
clarifying_info.a: A single plant in California produces all products: chilled, juice boxes, and frozen concentrate. It would be difficult to find another use for the plant without a major conversion.

framework: 1. Identify the options: (a) sell only the chilled juice business, (b) sell the entire juice division, (c) keep all businesses but restructure
2. Qualitative competitive analysis: assess Zephyr's market position, competitive disadvantages, and industry attractiveness
3. Product and cost analysis: examine ingredient mix vs. competitors and identify cost-reduction opportunities
4. Evaluate feasibility and synergies: manufacturing and advertising synergies across segments, plant utilization constraints
5. Recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: What is Zephyr's market share in chilled beverages and what does this mean competitively?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate Zephyr's implied market share: $120M chilled sales / $5B market = 2.4% (domestic share could differ; the casebook states 12% directly). The casebook states 12%, making Zephyr third behind 40% and 25% leaders. Candidate should recognize Zephyr is at a serious competitive disadvantage — it is smaller, less profitable, and unable to match the promotional spend (advertising, couponing, trade) that key retail customers value. Conclusion: weak competitive position.

math.setup: Zephyr chilled sales as a share of total market
steps: Implied share = $120M / $5,000M = 2.4% (note: casebook states 12%, suggesting the $5B figure may be a domestic subset or approximate)
math.answer: ~2–12% market share (casebook states 12%); third-largest player behind 40% and 25% leaders

questions.prompt: Why are Zephyr's chilled juices underperforming on cost?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about product composition vs. competitors. Zephyr uses elaborate blends (pear/peach base + exotic flavorings like cranberries, bananas, mangoes). The exotic flavorings (5% of inputs) cost about twice as much as standard inputs. Since all branded juices sell in the same price range, Zephyr cannot charge a premium for these extra-cost ingredients. The cost structure is higher without a revenue benefit — this is a key insight pointing toward reformulation.

steps: Flavorings are 5% of inputs and cost ~2x the standard ingredient price
If standard input cost = C per unit, the 5% flavoring portion costs 2C instead of C
Extra cost per unit = 5% × (2C − C) = 5% × C = 0.05C incremental per unit
math.answer: Zephyr incurs an incremental ~5% cost on its flavoring inputs with no corresponding revenue premium

questions.prompt: Evaluate each strategic option: sell chilled only, sell all juice, or keep and restructure.
questions.guidance: Option 1 — Sell chilled juice only: Would remove the loss-making segment, but Zephyr loses manufacturing synergies (shared California plant) and advertising synergies with juice boxes and frozen concentrate. A buyer may not be able to capture these synergies easily, potentially depressing the sale price. Option 2 — Sell all juice businesses: More feasible as a package since a buyer captures all synergies. However, the chilled underperformance makes the whole division less attractive; likely to command a low selling price. Option 3 — Keep chilled and reformulate ingredients: Most feasible economically. Competitors prove the market can be profitable. Zephyr's elaborate ingredient mix adds cost without adding revenue. Simplifying the recipe (e.g., moving toward citrus-based blends, reducing exotic flavorings) would cut costs. The California plant shared across all three product lines makes divestiture operationally complicated and costly.

brainstorming.prompt: What are additional risks and potential benefits for each of the three options?

categories.name: Sell chilled only — risks
ideas: Loss of manufacturing scale economies at the California plant
Loss of shared advertising and brand spend across Zephyr product lines
Remaining juice box and frozen businesses may become less competitive without scale
Buyer may demand significant discount given ongoing losses
Brand dilution if a new owner positions chilled Zephyr products differently

categories.name: Sell chilled only — benefits
ideas: Immediate elimination of loss-making segment
Management focus shifted to profitable juice box and frozen businesses
Cash proceeds can be reinvested in higher-margin segments or returned to parent

categories.name: Sell all juice — risks
ideas: Loses $600M in revenue from parent company (3% of total)
Synergies with other consumer goods divisions may be lost
Depressed sale price due to underperforming chilled segment dragging valuation
Potential job losses and reputational impact
Plant conversion costs if buyer does not want facility

categories.name: Sell all juice — benefits
ideas: Clean exit from a subscale, underperforming division
Buyer can potentially unlock synergies across all three juice formats
Frees management attention for core business
Avoids ongoing operational complexity of a three-format juice operation

categories.name: Keep and reformulate — risks
ideas: Reformulation may alienate existing loyal customers if taste changes
Time and R&D investment required before cost savings materialize
Competitors may respond with further promotional investment
No guarantee reformulation alone restores profitability without addressing scale disadvantage

categories.name: Keep and reformulate — benefits
ideas: Preserves manufacturing and advertising synergies
Addresses root cost issue (expensive exotic flavorings) without revenue sacrifice
Competitor profitability proves the model is viable at scale
Lowest disruption to current operations and workforce
Keeps option value — Zephyr can still divest later if reformulation fails

recommendation: Keep the chilled juice business and reformulate the ingredient mix. Zephyr's underperformance is primarily a cost problem, not a demand problem — the market is growing at GDP, brand matters, and competitors are assumed profitable. Zephyr's use of expensive exotic flavorings (costing ~2x standard inputs) at 5% of the blend adds cost with no revenue premium. Shifting toward a citrus-based formula aligned with market leaders would reduce input costs and likely restore profitability, while preserving the manufacturing and marketing synergies of a unified juice division.
risks: Customer taste preferences may favor the current blend; reformulation could reduce repeat purchases
The 12% market share puts Zephyr at a persistent promotional disadvantage vs. 40% and 25% leaders — reformulation alone may not close the profitability gap
The California plant is shared across all three formats; any structural change (sale of chilled) would require difficult plant reallocation
next_steps: Conduct consumer taste testing to determine how much of the exotic flavoring can be reduced without affecting repurchase intent
Model the cost savings from a reformulated recipe and verify whether they restore positive margins
Explore whether increased promotional trade spend (enabled by cost savings) can grow market share
Set a 12–18 month reformulation trial with clear go/no-go milestones; retain divestiture as a fallback if margins do not improve
